title: WPMS/1086/2004 of KM. NIDHI KEDIYAL Vs THE PRINCIPAL and ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARANCHAL AT
NAINITAL
W.P. NO. 1086 (MS) OF 2004
Km. Nidhi Kediyal ..................Petitioner.

Hon'ble Rajesh Tandon, J.
Heard Sri R.P. Nautiyal, counsel for the petitioner and Sri
Suresh Mishra, counsel for the respondents.
Briefly stated, the petitioner was given admission by the
respondent no.1 in session 2002 in the Senior Wing of NCC
Cadet Corps Course, conducted at G.P.P. Arya Girls Inter
College, Ram Nagar, District Nainital.
She was given admission after verifying all the relevant
forms required at the time of admission in the said course and
after satisfying with the procedural norms of admission, the
petitioner was admitted by awarding her registration no.
USW/2002/260390.
Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that during the
training course, she was performing extremely well in her
academics career and as such the respondent no. 1 was fully
satisfied with the conduct of the petitioner during the training
camp held since 25.08.2003 to 05.09.2003 at Hawalbagh, and
was awarded meritorious certificate on 05.09.2003 by camp
commandant confirming the petitioner's conduct to be good.
Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that all of a
sudden in the month of October, 2003 just after a week of the
conclusion of the first training camp at Hawalbagh, the

petitioner was taken a back, when the respondent no. 1 verbally
told the petitioner not to attend the course any further for the
best reasons, known to her. No reasons have been assigned to
the petitioner. Petitioner has submitted that her father has
made representations to the respondent no. 1 but no reply has
been given by the respondent. Further the representation dated
21st July, 2004 has not yet been disposed of.
Equity requires that once the petitioner was admitted in
the said training course, it is not open for the respondent to
discontinue the same during the course of the training and as
such considering the aforesaid fact, the respondent are
directed to consider the claim of the petitioner. In case, the
representation is not decided within a period of 10 days, the
petitioner shall continue the left over course of training.
Liberty is given to the petitioner to move a fresh
representation within a period of 10 days on the said
representation. The respondents are directed to pass a reasoned
order.
Subject to the aforesaid observation, the writ petition is
disposed of.
 (RAJESH TANDON, J.)
05.11.2004
P.S.R.
